en.title: China leverages short-video ecosystem, lower costs to carve out lead in AI video
en.summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence companies are carving out a distinct lead over their US rivals in video generation, leveraging vast short-video ecosystems, looser copyright rules and aggressive pricing to dominate an arena where compute alone does not dictate success, analysts say.

While US tech giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic continue to lead in frontier closed-source large language models (LLMs), Chinese firms are emerging as some of the most formidable competitors in the AI video space. Their edge stems from a combination of factors: an expansive base of user-generated content from platforms like Douyin and Kuaishou, more flexible copyright frameworks that allow training on diverse datasets, and a pricing strategy that undercuts Western counterparts by a significant margin. This has enabled Chinese players to iterate rapidly on video-generation models, producing outputs that rival or surpass US offerings in terms of realism, motion coherence, and creative flexibility—areas where raw computational power is necessary but not sufficient for success.

ja.title: 中国はショートビデオエコシステムと低コストを活用し、AI動画でリードを築く
ja.summary:
中国の人工知能企業は、動画生成の分野で米国の競合他社に対して明確なリードを築きつつある。アナリストによると、巨大なショート動画エコシステム、緩やかな著作権規制、そして攻勢的な価格設定を活用し、計算資源（コンピュート）だけでは成功が決まらない領域で支配的な地位を確立しているという。

OpenAIやAnthropicといった米国のハイテク大手が、最先端のクローズドソース大規模言語モデル（LLM）で引き続きリードする一方、中国企業はAI動画分野で最も手強い競争相手の一角として台頭している。
